hybrids.fertility: fertile=no; Male donkey (jack) x female horse (mare); source classification E. africanus asinus male x E. ferus caballus female, mapped to pilot GBIF names Equus asinus and Equus caballus; odd chromosome number makes gamete formation difficult, often infertile, rare mare mule births reported
fertile=no; Male horse (stallion) x female donkey (jenny); reciprocal cross to mule; most reports say hinnies are sterile
fertile=partial; Male lion x female tiger; exists only in captivity per source; male ligers sterile, female ligers fertile
hybrids.sex_specific_fertility: male ligers sterile, female ligers fertile

hybrids.fertility: fertile=partial; Male tiger x female lion; found only in captivity per source; male tigons sterile, females fertile

fertile=no; Zebra stallion x horse mare; source says generally no distinction made as to which zebra species is used, plains zebra Equus quagga used here as the pilot-list zebra; zorse is sterile per source
fertile=partial; Domestic cattle usually male x American bison usually female in managed breeding programs; female offspring proved fertile, rarely so for males
hybrids.sex_specific_fertility: female offspring proved fertile, rarely so for males

hybrids.fertility: fertile=yes; Male false killer whale x female bottlenose dolphin; born in captivity and reported in the wild; Kekaimalu was fertile and gave birth in 1991 and 2004; both parents have 44 chromosomes
fertile=no; Male dromedary camel x female llama, produced via artificial insemination at the Camel Reproduction Centre in Dubai; first cama born 14 January 1998; camas are sterile per source note
fertile=yes; Grizzly bear father x polar bear mother in the confirmed 2006 wild case; hybrids have occurred both in captivity and in the wild; zoo hybrids have proven fertile per source

fertile=unknown; Second-generation hybrid: male lion x female liger (lion x tiger hybrid); mother is a liger, not a pure species, so parent2 is a hybrid, not a pilot-list species alone; first such hybrid born 1943 at Hellabrunn Zoo; liliger fertility not stated in source
fertile=partial; Male serval x female domestic cat, first hybrid 7 April 1986; F1/F2 males sterile, females fertile, later generations fertile
hybrids.sex_specific_fertility: F1/F2 males sterile, females fertile; later generations fertile

hybrids.fertility: fertile=partial; Asian leopard cat x domestic cat; early-generation males sterile, females fertile
fertile=partial; Male caracal x female domestic cat; first recorded at Moscow Zoo 1998, first planned litter male caracal x Abyssinian females; F1 males sterile, females fertile

fertile=yes; Gray wolf x domestic dog; both directions occur in the wild and in breeding. Note: domestic dog's GBIF accepted name is also Canis lupus, so both parents resolve to the same GBIF species; Canis familiaris is used here for the dog parent as in the hybrid source
fertile=yes; Coyote x gray wolf; eastern coyote/wolf/dog admixture is also reported, but this row is the coyote x gray wolf cross, both Tier 1 parents

fertile=yes; Male coyote x female dog; hybrids of both sexes are fertile and can be bred through four generations per source. Note: domestic dog's GBIF accepted name is Canis lupus; Canis familiaris is used here for the dog parent as in the hybrid source, as with wolfdog
fertile=unknown; Male leopard x female lion (lioness); occurs only in captivity; first documented at Kolhapur 1910, later at Hanshin Park, Japan, 1959/1961; fertility of leopons not stated in source
fertile=unknown; Jaguar x lion cross in captivity (naming convention: father species first); fertility not stated in source
fertile=unknown; Male jaguar x female leopard; crossbreeding between jaguars and leopards in captivity has been documented; reverse cross is called leguar
fertile=unknown; Cougar x leopard; both pairings (male cougar x female leopard and reverse) have produced offspring; hybrids show dwarfism, most did not reach adulthood
fertile=no; Zebra stallion x donkey mare (zebroid); zebroids are sterile per source, as with zorse

fertile=yes; Bactrian camel x dromedary; practised for over two thousand years along the Silk Road for stronger, more cold-tolerant pack animals; hybrid camels are fertile and used in further breeding
fertile=unknown; First-generation hybrid blue-and-gold macaw x scarlet macaw; first produced in captivity at Catalina Bird Park, 1940
fertile=unknown; First-generation hybrid blue-and-gold macaw x green-winged macaw; bred only in captivity, rarely found in the wild
fertile=unknown; Male beluga x female narwhal; confirmed from a skull found in West Greenland, genetically confirmed as a first-generation hybrid; fertility not stated
fertile=partial; Domestic cattle x European bison (wisent); first created 1847 in Poland; first-generation males sterile, females fertile and can be backcrossed
hybrids.sex_specific_fertility: first-generation males sterile, females fertile and can be backcrossed

hybrids.fertility: fertile=partial; Yak x domestic cow; male dzo sterile, female dzomo fertile and can be backcrossed; larger and stronger than either parent (heterosis)
hybrids.sex_specific_fertility: male dzo sterile, female dzomo fertile and can be backcrossed

hybrids.fertility: fertile=partial; Yak bulls x bison cows in 1920s hybridisation experiments; only female hybrids were found fertile (Haldane's rule); experiments discontinued 1928
hybrids.sex_specific_fertility: only female hybrids were found fertile (Haldane's rule)

hybrids.fertility: fertile=yes; Male llama x female alpaca; most common South American camelid hybrid; fertile and capable of back-crossing with parent species

fertile=partial; Male sheep x female goat; Botswana 2000 case: live male offspring with 57 chromosomes, infertile; New Zealand female hybrid was fertile when mated with a ram, so fertility is partial overall
hybrids.sex_specific_fertility: Botswana 2000 live male offspring with 57 chromosomes, infertile; New Zealand female hybrid was fertile when mated with a ram; fertility partial overall; male/female cases differ

hybrids.fertility: fertile=unknown; Second-generation hybrid: male tiger x female liger (lion x tiger); first tiligers born 16 August 2007; mother is a liger, so parent2 is hybrid:liger

rules.rule_text: A fusion must use exactly one body_plan value from the Tier 1 allowed set: quadruped, biped, biped|winged, winged, finned, multi_legged, serpentine, radial.
rules.test_method: Check fusion body_plan is in the allowed set and is a single value.
rules.basis: radial added 2026-10-28 as a project decision for moon_jellyfish

rules.rule_text: A fusion's covering must be a covering of at least one donor parent (fur, feathers, scales, skin, exoskeleton, shell).
rules.test_method: Check fusion covering is in the union of parents' coverings.

rules.rule_text: A fusion may not assign two different coverings to the same body region without naming the region for each.
rules.test_method: Check covering list per region; flag any unlabelled double covering.

rules.rule_text: A winged fusion must have a winged or biped|winged donor; wings cannot be invented from a finned or serpentine donor alone.
rules.test_method: Check at least one parent body_plan contains 'winged'.

rules.rule_text: A finned fusion must have a finned donor; fins cannot be invented from a quadruped donor alone.
rules.test_method: Check at least one parent body_plan is 'finned'.

rules.rule_text: A serpentine fusion must have a serpentine donor; a limbless body cannot be invented from a quadruped donor alone.
rules.test_method: Check at least one parent body_plan is 'serpentine'.

rules.rule_text: A shelled fusion must have a shelled donor (covering=shell); a shell cannot be invented from a fur or feather donor alone.
rules.test_method: Check at least one parent covering is 'shell'.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's head count must be stated explicitly; the default is one head, and multi-headed designs must name the donor for each extra head.
rules.test_method: Check head_count field is present and >=1; if >1, check donor attribution.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's body_mass, if stated, must lie within the minimum-to-maximum interval spanned by its parents' Tier 1 body_mass ranges (using a single average as both endpoints).
rules.test_method: Parse parent mass ranges; check fusion mass is inside the spanned interval.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's body_length, if stated, must lie within the interval spanned by its parents' Tier 1 body_length ranges.
rules.test_method: Parse parent length ranges; check fusion length is inside the spanned interval.

rules.rule_text: A parent mass ratio above 1000x (larger parent maximum / smaller parent minimum) is an extreme-size conflict and must be flagged, not silently averaged.
rules.test_method: Compute max/min ratio; flag if >1000.

rules.rule_text: A source range must be kept as a range in any fusion table; a midpoint must never be computed from a range.
rules.test_method: Check value fields for ranges are stored as 'low-high', never a single computed midpoint.

rules.rule_text: If a source gives only a single average mass, store it as a single value with notes 'average; no range', never invent a range around it.
rules.test_method: Check single-value rows carry the 'average; no range' note.

rules.rule_text: If a source gives only a maximum mass or length, leave the fusion measurement blank with a note; a maximum is not a range or an average.
rules.test_method: Check maxima-only cases are blank, not stored as ranges.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's mass and length must use kg and m respectively; gram or cm source values must be converted and the conversion noted.
rules.test_method: Check units are kg/m; check converted rows carry a conversion note.

rules.rule_text: Implausible source values (e.g. a 10.7 m leopard cat, a 12 m anaconda, a 0.0001 kg adult lobster) must be left blank with an explanatory note, never used.
rules.test_method: Check implausible-value rows are blank with notes, per Tier 1 failure findings.

rules.rule_text: A real hybrid's parents must be named by scientific name and role (father/mother), exactly as in Tier 1 hybrids.csv.
rules.test_method: Check parent1_scientific, parent2_scientific and roles are present.

rules.rule_text: A reciprocal cross (swapped father/mother) is a different hybrid from the original cross and must be recorded separately.
rules.test_method: Check mule vs hinny, liger vs tigon are distinct rows.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid whose parent is itself a hybrid must be written hybrid:<hybrid_id>, never as a pure species.
rules.test_method: Check liliger parent2 is 'hybrid:liger'.

rules.rule_text: Fertility must be recorded as yes, no, partial or unknown; 'partial' means one sex fertile and the other sterile, as in liger and tigon.
rules.test_method: Check fertility value is in the allowed set and matches the source note.

rules.rule_text: A captive-only hybrid must be marked captive_only, not documented, even if it is well known.
rules.test_method: Check confidence is captive_only for liger, tigon, zorse, cama and liliger.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid with an odd chromosome number or mismatched parent chromosome counts must be flagged as likely infertile unless the source states fertility.
rules.test_method: Check chromosome note present when fertility=no is claimed on that basis.

rules.rule_text: A fusion design inspired by a real hybrid must not claim the real hybrid's fertility unless its parents and cross direction match that hybrid exactly.
rules.test_method: Check fusion parents and direction against the real hybrid row before copying fertility.

rules.rule_text: A second-generation hybrid (hybrid x pure species) must be marked as such and must not be presented as a first-generation cross.
rules.test_method: Check generation field; liliger is second-generation.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's movement list must be a subset of the union of its parents' Tier 1 movement values.
rules.test_method: Check every fusion movement token appears in at least one parent's movement list.

rules.rule_text: A fusion may not claim 'fly' unless at least one parent moves by flying.
rules.test_method: Check 'fly' in fusion movement implies 'fly' in a parent movement list.

rules.rule_text: A fusion may not claim 'swim' unless at least one parent moves by swimming.
rules.test_method: Check 'swim' in fusion movement implies 'swim' in a parent movement list.

rules.rule_text: A serpentine donor's movement, where Tier 1 records it as blank because slithering is not in the allowed list, must be recorded as a gap, not as walk or run.
rules.test_method: Check serpentine fusions do not invent walk/run from a blank movement row.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's active_time must be a subset of the union of its parents' active_time values, or be marked as a design choice with a note.
rules.test_method: Check active_time tokens against parents, or check design-choice note.

rules.rule_text: A diurnal-only fusion must not be built from two nocturnal-only parents without a note explaining the change.
rules.test_method: Check diurnal claim against parent active_time values.

rules.rule_text: A fusion that combines a flying parent and a swimming parent must state which medium is primary; it may not claim both at full competence without a note.
rules.test_method: Check primary_medium field for fly+swim fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's habitat list must overlap at least one habitat of each parent, or the non-overlap must be flagged as a habitat conflict.
rules.test_method: Compute habitat intersection per parent; flag empty intersections.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's climate list must overlap at least one climate of each parent, or the non-overlap must be flagged as a climate conflict.
rules.test_method: Compute climate intersection per parent; flag empty intersections.

rules.rule_text: A marine-only fusion must not be built from a terrestrial-only parent without a habitat-change note.
rules.test_method: Check marine claim against parent habitat lists.

rules.rule_text: A polar-climate fusion must have a polar donor or a stated insulation mechanism; polar cannot be invented from tropical-only parents.
rules.test_method: Check polar claim against parent climate lists.

rules.rule_text: A fusion combining a freshwater parent and a marine parent must state its salinity tolerance; it may not be assumed to live in both.
rules.test_method: Check salinity note for freshwater+marine fusions.

rules.rule_text: A desert fusion must have a desert donor or a stated water-conservation mechanism.
rules.test_method: Check desert claim against parent habitat lists.

rules.rule_text: Habitat values must use the Tier 1 allowed set (grassland, forest, desert, mountain, tundra, wetland, freshwater, marine); free-text habitats must be mapped or left blank with a note.
rules.test_method: Check habitat tokens are in the allowed set.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's diet must be a diet of at least one parent, or a stated intermediate (e.g. omnivore from carnivore x herbivore) with a note.
rules.test_method: Check diet against parent diets, or check intermediate note.

rules.rule_text: A carnivore x herbivore fusion must not be recorded as purely carnivore or purely herbivore without a note; the default intermediate is omnivore.
rules.test_method: Check diet for carnivore x herbivore fusions.

rules.rule_text: A diet value outside the Tier 1 allowed set (carnivore, herbivore, omnivore, insectivore, piscivore) must be mapped to the closest allowed value with a note, or left blank.
rules.test_method: Check diet tokens are in the allowed set; check mapping notes (e.g. planktivore -> omnivore).

rules.rule_text: A fusion's metabolic_rate, if stated, must be sourced and in watts; a value that is implausibly low for the fusion's mass must be left blank with a note.
rules.test_method: Check metabolic_rate units are W; check implausible values are blank with notes.

rules.rule_text: A structured diet field that contradicts the source's own descriptive text must be resolved in favour of the text, with the discrepancy noted.
rules.test_method: Check Bactrian camel-type cases: diet follows text, discrepancy noted.

rules.rule_text: A fusion must not average metabolic rates across parents; if no single source value exists, leave it blank or list parent values separately.
rules.test_method: Check no averaged metabolic_rate value is stored.

rules.rule_text: An insectivore fusion must have an insectivore donor or a stated insect-eating mechanism; insectivory cannot be invented from a large-carnivore donor alone.
rules.test_method: Check insectivore claim against parent diets.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature row must name its culture, its component animals, and the part each animal contributes.
rules.test_method: Check culture, component_animals and component_parts are all present.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with any human component must have has_human_part=yes; all others must have no.
rules.test_method: Check has_human_part against component_animals containing 'human'.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature's component animals must be real animals or 'human'; invented component species must not be used.
rules.test_method: Check every component animal is a real animal name or human.

rules.rule_text: A creature with three or more component animals must list each animal's parts separately, not as a single mixed list.
rules.test_method: Check component_parts uses 'animal:parts' segments per animal.

rules.rule_text: A mythological part that has no Tier 1 donor (e.g. a scorpion sting on a lion body) must be marked as mythological, not as a Tier 1 body part.
rules.test_method: Check mythological-only parts are flagged, not merged into body_parts.csv.

rules.rule_text: A creature's culture must be the culture of its earliest well-documented form, not the culture of a later retelling, unless the retelling is noted.
rules.test_method: Check culture field against the source page's origin section.

rules.rule_text: A shapeshifting creature (e.g. werewolf, selkie, kelpie) must be recorded with both forms, not as a single fixed composite.
rules.test_method: Check shapeshifters list both human and animal forms.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A fusion design must pass all hard rules in this file before it is marked PASS; a single hard-rule conflict makes it FAIL or FLAG, never PASS with a note.
rules.test_method: Run the test harness; check PASS requires zero hard conflicts.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A fusion with a body_plan conflict (e.g. finned x quadruped with no amphibious design note) must be flagged, not silently resolved by picking one parent's plan.
rules.test_method: Check body_plan conflicts are flagged in test output.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A fusion with no habitat overlap with a parent must be flagged as a habitat conflict in the test output.
rules.test_method: Check habitat intersection is computed and empty intersections are flagged.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A fusion with a mass ratio above 1000x between parents must be flagged as an extreme-size conflict.
rules.test_method: Check mass ratio is computed and >1000x is flagged.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A test round is clean only if every test fusion is evaluated, every rule check runs, and no fusion has a missing-data gap that was not logged.
rules.test_method: Check test_rounds.csv: all fusions evaluated, gaps logged.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A design that uses a blank Tier 1 trait (value left blank for implausibility or absence) must treat that trait as unknown, never fill it from memory.
rules.test_method: Check blank-trait fusions carry 'unknown' for that trait, not an invented value.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A failure mode must name the failed rule, the fusion or trait it applies to, and a mitigation or a reason it cannot be mitigated.
rules.test_method: Check failure_modes.csv rows have rule_id, applies_to and mitigation fields.

rules.area_name: Fusion Design, Viability and Failure Modes
rules.rule_text: A rule that is contradicted by a verified source must be retired or sharpened, not kept active with a note; retired rules are logged in decisions_log.md.
rules.test_method: Check active rules list contains no rule contradicted by a VERIFIED finding.

rules.rule_text: A fusion combining a tundra parent and a tropical parent must state its thermal range; it may not be assumed to live in both extremes without a note.
rules.test_method: Check thermal-range note for tundra+tropical fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a wetland parent must not be recorded as purely terrestrial or purely aquatic without a note on its water dependence.
rules.test_method: Check water-dependence note for wetland fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's leg count must match its body_plan: quadruped = 4 legs, biped = 2 legs, serpentine = 0 legs, multi_legged = more than 4 legs.
rules.test_method: Check leg count against body_plan.

rules.rule_text: A fusion may not combine a shell with wings on the same body without naming how the shell and wings are arranged.
rules.test_method: Check shell+wing fusions carry an arrangement note.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's tail, if claimed, must come from a donor that has a tail in its Tier 1 description or be marked as a design addition.
rules.test_method: Check tail claim against donor descriptions or design-addition note.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a horn, antler or tusk must name the donor for that structure; horns, antlers and tusks are not interchangeable.
rules.test_method: Check horn/antler/tusk donor is named and matches the structure type.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's brain_mass, if stated, must be in grams and must not be confused with body_mass in kilograms.
rules.test_method: Check brain_mass units are g and body_mass units are kg.

rules.rule_text: A specimen_body_mass is a single specimen's mass, not a species range, and must be labelled as such with its source reference.
rules.test_method: Check specimen rows carry a specimen label and reference.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid whose notes mention chromosome differences must carry that chromosome note in its inheritance rows.
rules.test_method: Check chromosome notes are present where hybrids.csv mentions them.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid whose notes mention backcrossing must record which parent species it can be backcrossed with.
rules.test_method: Check backcross parent is named where hybrids.csv mentions backcrossing.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid whose notes mention heterosis (larger/stronger than either parent) must record heterosis as a note, not as a measured mass.
rules.test_method: Check heterosis is a note, not a mass value.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid whose notes give a first-record date or place must record that date/place, not a generic 'historic' label.
rules.test_method: Check first-record date/place is present where hybrids.csv gives it.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid with unknown fertility must not be used as evidence that a fusion with the same parents will be fertile.
rules.test_method: Check unknown-fertility hybrids are not cited as fertility evidence.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid name that follows the father-first naming convention must be checked against the source; father-first is a convention, not a proof of parentage.
rules.test_method: Check parentage against hybrids.csv, not against the name alone.

rules.rule_text: A fusion may claim movement 'walk' only if at least one parent's Tier 1 movement includes 'walk'.
rules.test_method: Check 'walk' in fusion movement implies 'walk' in a parent movement list.

rules.rule_text: A fusion that walks and swims must state whether it walks on land and swims in water, or whether one medium is primary.
rules.test_method: Check primary_medium for walk+swim fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion that climbs must have a climbing donor; climbing cannot be inferred from walking alone.
rules.test_method: Check climb claim against parent movement lists.

rules.rule_text: A fusion that burrows must have a burrowing donor; burrowing cannot be inferred from walking alone.
rules.test_method: Check burrow claim against parent movement lists.

rules.rule_text: A fusion that glides must have a gliding donor; gliding is not the same as flying and must not be recorded as fly.
rules.test_method: Check glide claim against parent movement lists; check glide is not stored as fly.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with no movement donor for a claimed movement must be flagged, even if the movement seems plausible for the body plan.
rules.test_method: Check every movement token against parents; flag unmatched tokens.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's senses (e.g. echolocation, electroreception) must come from a donor with that sense; senses are not transferred by body plan alone.
rules.test_method: Check sense claims against donor traits or mark as design additions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion recorded in both freshwater and marine habitats must state its salinity tolerance explicitly.
rules.test_method: Check salinity note for freshwater+marine fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion recorded at both high altitude and sea level must state its elevation range explicitly.
rules.test_method: Check elevation range for mountain+marine fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion recorded in a wetland must state whether it is aquatic, semi-aquatic or terrestrial in that wetland.
rules.test_method: Check wetland dependence note.

rules.rule_text: A fusion recorded with diet 'carnivore' must have at least one parent whose Tier 1 diet includes 'carnivore', or a stated intermediate with a note.
rules.test_method: Check 'carnivore' against parent diets or intermediate note.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's metabolic_rate must not be taken from a different species' row; metabolic rates are species-specific in Tier 1.
rules.test_method: Check metabolic_rate source animal matches the fusion donor.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a metabolic_rate below 1 W and a body_mass above 1 kg must be flagged as implausible, as with serval 1.44 W.
rules.test_method: Check metabolic_rate against body_mass; flag implausible combinations.

rules.rule_text: A fusion that is a piscivore must have a fish-eating donor; piscivory is not the same as general carnivory and must not be merged into it.
rules.test_method: Check piscivore claim against parent diets.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's diet must be recorded per life stage if the parents' diets differ by life stage; a single adult diet must not be assumed for juveniles.
rules.test_method: Check life-stage diet note where parents differ by stage.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with no diet donor and no intermediate note must have diet left blank, not filled from the fusion's body plan.
rules.test_method: Check diet blank cases are blank, not inferred.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's energy budget must be consistent with its mass: a very large fusion with a very low metabolic rate must be flagged.
rules.test_method: Check mass/metabolic consistency; flag large-mass low-rate fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's diet must be checked against its habitat: a marine fusion recorded as herbivore must have a marine plant-eating donor or a note.
rules.test_method: Check marine herbivore claims against donors.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with 1 component animal(s) must list exactly 1 component animal(s) in component_animals, with parts for each.
rules.test_method: Count component_animals; check parts per animal.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with has_human_part=yes must list 'human' in component_animals; a creature listing human must not have has_human_part=no.
rules.test_method: Check has_human_part against component_animals containing human.

rules.rule_text: A mythological deity (e.g. Anubis, Garuda) must be recorded as a deity form, not as a wild animal species, in mythology_parts.csv.
rules.test_method: Check deity rows are not merged into the species catalog.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature that is a shapeshifter must list both forms in component_parts, not a single fixed form.
rules.test_method: Check shapeshifter rows list both forms.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with a human head and an animal body must record the head donor and body donor separately.
rules.test_method: Check head/body donors are separate segments.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with an animal head and a human body must record the head donor and body donor separately.
rules.test_method: Check head/body donors are separate segments.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with wings must record the wing donor; wings must not be assumed from a bird component without a wings segment.
rules.test_method: Check wings segment is present where wings are claimed.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with a tail sting or venom must record the sting/venom donor; venom must not be assumed from a scorpion tail alone without a note.
rules.test_method: Check sting/venom donor segment.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with multiple heads must record the head count and the donor for each head.
rules.test_method: Check head count and donors for multi-headed creatures.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature's parts must be plausible for its components: a fish component must not contribute wings, and a bird component must not contribute a tail fin, without a note.
rules.test_method: Check parts against component animal types.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with a human part must not be used as a species donor in body_parts.csv; human parts are mythology-only.
rules.test_method: Check human-part creatures are not in body_parts.csv.

rules.rule_text: A fusion in 'tundra|marine' habitat must state its sea-ice dependence if marine is retained; tundra|marine is not a generic cold habitat.
rules.test_method: Check sea-ice note for tundra|marine fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion combining an 'arid' climate parent with a 'polar' climate parent must state its thermal range; arid and polar are not interchangeable cold/dry labels.
rules.test_method: Check thermal-range note for arid+polar fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a 'freshwater|marine' parent must state its life-stage habitat if it is anadromous; freshwater|marine does not mean it lives in both at all times.
rules.test_method: Check life-stage note for freshwater|marine fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a 'mountain|freshwater' parent must state both its elevation range and its water dependence; mountain and freshwater are separate requirements.
rules.test_method: Check elevation and water notes for mountain|freshwater fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion in 'forest|wetland' habitat must state its water dependence in forest as well as in wetland; forest cover does not imply wetland water.
rules.test_method: Check water-dependence note for forest|wetland fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion combining a 'tundra|desert|grassland' parent with a forest-only parent must state which of the three open habitats it actually uses; a broad parent range is not a fusion range.
rules.test_method: Check habitat subset note for broad-range fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion in 'desert|mountain' habitat must state both its water-conservation mechanism and its elevation range; desert and mountain are separate constraints.
rules.test_method: Check water and elevation notes for desert|mountain fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a 'temperate|tropical|polar' parent must not be recorded as living in all three climates unless each climate is separately justified; a broad parent range is not evidence for all three in the fusion.
rules.test_method: Check per-climate justification for broad-climate fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion combining a serpentine parent with a quadruped parent must state which body plan is primary and how limbs are handled; it may not be recorded as both serpentine and quadruped.
rules.test_method: Check primary body_plan and limb note for serpentine+quadruped fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a multi-legged parent must state the leg count or leg-count range used; 'multiple legs' is not a count.
rules.test_method: Check leg-count field for multi-legged fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a shelled parent and a fur parent must state whether the shell covers the whole body or a region; a whole-body shell and whole-body fur cannot both be claimed for the same region.
rules.test_method: Check shell coverage region for shell+fur fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's specimen_body_mass, if stated, must be a single specimen value with sex, sample size and reference, never a species range relabelled as a specimen.
rules.test_method: Check specimen rows carry sex, sample size and reference.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's brain_mass, if stated, must be in grams and must not be averaged across specimens; list specimens separately.
rules.test_method: Check brain_mass units are g and no averaged value is stored.

rules.rule_text: A fusion combining a parent with a body_mass range and a parent with only a single average mass must use the spanned interval, not a range invented around the average.
rules.test_method: Check spanned interval calculation for range+average fusions.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid's parent Tier 1 match must be recorded separately from its cross: a parent that resolves to the same GBIF species as another parent (e.g. dog and wolf) is not two distinct species for fusion purposes.
rules.test_method: Check parent Tier 1 match field for wolfdog-type hybrids.

rules.rule_text: A second-generation hybrid must name its hybrid parent by hybrid:<hybrid_id> in every table, not only in hybrids.csv.
rules.test_method: Check hybrid parent references in all tables use hybrid:<id>.

rules.rule_text: A hybrid with heterosis (larger/stronger than either parent, as in dzo) must be marked as heterosis, not as a normal mass interval, when its mass is used in a fusion.
rules.test_method: Check heterosis note for dzo-type fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a 'fly|walk|glide' parent must state whether glide is used; glide is not the same as powered flight and must not be recorded as fly without a note.
rules.test_method: Check glide note for glide-capable fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a burrowing parent must state burrowing as a separate movement token; burrow is not transferred by walk|run alone.
rules.test_method: Check burrow token for burrowing fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion combining a diurnal parent with a nocturnal parent must state its active_time as the overlap or as a design choice with a note; it may not be recorded as both fully diurnal and fully nocturnal.
rules.test_method: Check active_time overlap or design note for diurnal+nocturnal fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion with a 'carnivore|piscivore' parent must state whether fish are included; piscivore is not automatically included in carnivore.
rules.test_method: Check fish-inclusion note for carnivore|piscivore fusions.

rules.rule_text: A fusion's metabolic_rate from AnimalTraits must carry its specimen sex, sample size and reference; a bare watt value without provenance does not count.
rules.test_method: Check metabolic specimen provenance.

rules.rule_text: An insectivore fusion must state its prey size class; insectivore does not cover all invertebrate prey (e.g. large crustaceans) without a note.
rules.test_method: Check prey-size note for insectivore fusions.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature with nine or more component animals (e.g. navagunjara) must list every component's parts; a summary 'nine animals' does not count as a parts list.
rules.test_method: Check parts list length for multi-component creatures.

rules.rule_text: A shapeshifting mythological creature must be recorded with both forms and the trigger or condition for shifting, if the source states one; a single fixed form does not count.
rules.test_method: Check both forms for shapeshifters.

rules.rule_text: A mythological creature that is also a deity (e.g. anubis, garuda) must be marked as deity as well as creature; deity status changes how its parts are used in a fusion.
rules.test_method: Check deity flag for deity-creatures.

rules.rule_text: A parent with active_time 'unrecorded' adds no tokens. The fusion's active_time is built from the other parents' values under R-A4-05, R-A4-06 and R-A4-P03. If every parent is 'unrecorded', the fusion's active_time is 'unrecorded' and the app shows it as 'activity pattern unknown'. 'unrecorded' never blocks a fusion and is never combined with other tokens.
rules.test_method: Drop 'unrecorded' parents, then check the remaining parents as usual; if none remain, check the fusion value is exactly 'unrecorded'.

failure_modes.example: Finned x quadruped fusion with no amphibious design note
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag as FAIL; add an amphibious design note or change a parent.

failure_modes.example: Fusion covering matches neither parent
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag as FAIL; pick a parent covering or name a new region.

failure_modes.example: Parent mass ratio above 1000x
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag as extreme-size conflict; do not average.

failure_modes.example: Source value used despite being implausible (e.g. 10.7 m leopard cat)
failure_modes.mitigation: Remove value, leave blank with note.

failure_modes.example: Midpoint computed from a source range
failure_modes.mitigation: Restore the range; delete the midpoint.

failure_modes.example: Fusion assumed fertile without matching a real hybrid cross
failure_modes.mitigation: Set fertility to unknown until the cross is matched.

failure_modes.example: Liliger-type parent recorded as a pure species
failure_modes.mitigation: Rewrite parent as hybrid:<hybrid_id>.

failure_modes.example: Fly claimed without a flying parent
failure_modes.mitigation: Remove fly or add a flying donor.

failure_modes.example: Serpentine blank movement filled as walk/run
failure_modes.mitigation: Restore blank/unknown; log the gap.

failure_modes.example: Fusion habitat overlaps neither parent habitat
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag as habitat conflict; change habitat or parents.

failure_modes.example: Fusion climate overlaps neither parent climate
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag as climate conflict; change climate or parents.

failure_modes.example: Fusion diet matches neither parent and has no intermediate note
failure_modes.mitigation: Set diet to a parent diet or omnivore with a note.

failure_modes.example: Metabolic rate implausibly low for mass used as if valid
failure_modes.mitigation: Leave blank with note, as with serval 1.44 W.

failure_modes.example: Structured diet field contradicts source text and is used anyway
failure_modes.mitigation: Follow the text; note the discrepancy.

failure_modes.example: Mythological creature with a human component marked has_human_part=no
failure_modes.mitigation: Correct to yes.

failure_modes.example: Scorpion sting or other myth-only part merged into body_parts.csv
failure_modes.mitigation: Remove from body_parts; keep in mythology_parts only.

failure_modes.example: Test fusion evaluated with a blank trait treated as a value
failure_modes.mitigation: Log the gap; treat the trait as unknown.

failure_modes.example: Fusion marked PASS despite a hard-rule conflict
failure_modes.mitigation: Change to FAIL/FLAG; PASS requires zero hard conflicts.

failure_modes.example: Rule contradicted by a verified source kept active
failure_modes.mitigation: Retire or sharpen the rule; log in decisions_log.md.

failure_modes.example: Fusion parents differ by 10-100x in mass, treated as if similar in size
failure_modes.mitigation: Record the ratio and check the design for size consequences.

failure_modes.example: Fusion parents differ by 100-1000x in mass, averaged without a note
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag as a large-size design; do not average.

failure_modes.example: Fusion parents differ by more than 1000x in mass
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag as extreme-size; redesign or record as a stress test.

failure_modes.example: Metabolic rate implausibly low for mass used as valid
failure_modes.mitigation: Leave blank with a note, as with serval 1.44 W.

failure_modes.example: Metabolic rate recorded in a unit other than watts
failure_modes.mitigation: Convert to watts with a note or leave blank.

failure_modes.example: Mythology creature listing human marked no in a later cycle
failure_modes.mitigation: Correct to yes and log the correction.

failure_modes.example: Fertility inferred from a hybrid name rather than hybrids.csv
failure_modes.mitigation: Check hybrids.csv; do not infer from the name.

failure_modes.example: Fusion marked PASS with an unlogged data gap
failure_modes.mitigation: Change to GAP and log the gap.

failure_modes.example: Blank trait treated as zero or as a parent value
failure_modes.mitigation: Restore unknown and log the gap.

failure_modes.example: Multi-headed fusion with no head count or donors
failure_modes.mitigation: Record head count and donors.

failure_modes.example: Single head assumed for a multi-headed creature
failure_modes.mitigation: Check the creature; record the actual head count.

failure_modes.example: Tundra x tropical fusion with no thermal range
failure_modes.mitigation: Record a thermal range or flag the conflict.

failure_modes.example: Wetland fusion with no water-dependence note
failure_modes.mitigation: Record water dependence.

failure_modes.example: Active_time changed from parents without a design note
failure_modes.mitigation: Record the change as a design choice.

failure_modes.example: Fly+swim fusion with no primary medium
failure_modes.mitigation: Record a primary medium.

failure_modes.example: Diet token outside the allowed set used without mapping
failure_modes.mitigation: Map to the closest allowed value with a note, or leave blank.

failure_modes.example: Fusion with fur and shell on the same region, no region labels
failure_modes.mitigation: Label covering by region or drop one covering.

failure_modes.example: Fins claimed from a quadruped parent only
failure_modes.mitigation: Add a finned donor or remove fins.

failure_modes.example: Limbless body claimed from a quadruped parent only
failure_modes.mitigation: Add a serpentine donor or keep legs.

failure_modes.example: Shell claimed from a fur parent only
failure_modes.mitigation: Add a shelled donor or remove the shell.

failure_modes.example: Fusion mass above the larger parent maximum or below the smaller parent minimum
failure_modes.mitigation: Bring mass inside the spanned interval or flag as extrapolation.

failure_modes.example: Fusion length outside the parents spanned length interval
failure_modes.mitigation: Bring length inside the interval or flag as extrapolation.

failure_modes.example: Single average mass expanded into an invented range
failure_modes.mitigation: Restore the single average with an average note.

failure_modes.example: Maximum-only mass or length stored as a range
failure_modes.mitigation: Leave blank with a maxima-only note.

failure_modes.example: Gram or cm source value stored as kg or m without conversion
failure_modes.mitigation: Convert and note the conversion.

failure_modes.example: Hybrid parent named without father/mother role
failure_modes.mitigation: Add the role from the source.

failure_modes.example: Mule and hinny recorded as the same hybrid
failure_modes.mitigation: Split reciprocal crosses into separate rows.

failure_modes.example: Captive-only hybrid recorded as documented in the wild
failure_modes.mitigation: Correct confidence to captive_only.

failure_modes.example: Infertility claimed without the chromosome note that supports it
failure_modes.mitigation: Add the chromosome note or change fertility to unknown.

failure_modes.example: Liger fertility copied to a lion x tiger fusion with swapped parents
failure_modes.mitigation: Match parents and direction before copying fertility.

failure_modes.example: Second-generation hybrid recorded as first-generation
failure_modes.mitigation: Mark generation as second-generation.

failure_modes.example: Fly claimed without a flying parent
failure_modes.mitigation: Remove fly or add a flying donor.

failure_modes.example: Swim claimed without a swimming parent
failure_modes.mitigation: Remove swim or add a swimming donor.

failure_modes.example: Diurnal fusion built from two nocturnal parents without a note
failure_modes.mitigation: Add a design-choice note or change active_time.

failure_modes.example: Marine-only fusion from a terrestrial-only parent without a note
failure_modes.mitigation: Add a habitat-change note or change a parent.

failure_modes.example: Polar climate claimed from tropical-only parents without insulation
failure_modes.mitigation: Add a polar donor or an insulation mechanism.

design_principles.principle: Start from one parent's body_plan; do not blend two incompatible plans without an explicit design note.
Pick covering from a donor; do not invent a new covering for a fusion.
Keep fusion mass inside the parents' spanned mass interval, or flag it as a design extrapolation.
Keep fusion length inside the parents' spanned length interval, or flag it as a design extrapolation.
Flag parent mass ratios above 1000x as extreme-size designs; do not average them away.
Use the real hybrid's cross direction when copying a real hybrid design; reciprocal crosses differ.
Record fertility as yes/no/partial/unknown; never assume a fusion is fertile.
Movement for a fusion must come from its parents; do not add fly or swim without a donor.
State a primary medium for fly+swim fusions; do not claim full competence in both without a note.
Require habitat overlap with each parent, or flag the habitat conflict explicitly.
Require climate overlap with each parent, or flag the climate conflict explicitly.
Diet for a fusion must come from a parent or be a stated intermediate (omnivore).
Do not average metabolic rates; list parent values separately or leave blank.
When a source's structured field contradicts its own text, follow the text and note the discrepancy.
Mythological designs must list culture, components and parts per animal.
Mark has_human_part=yes for any mythological design with a human component.
Shapeshifters must be designed with both forms, not a single fixed composite.
A fusion that fails a hard rule is FAIL or FLAG, never PASS with a note.
Treat blank Tier 1 traits as unknown, never fill them from memory.
Implausible values are left blank with notes, in every table, without exception.
Ranges are kept as ranges; midpoints are never computed.
When designing a fusion with a stated metabolic_rate, keep the rate in watts and attach its source reference; do not convert it to a mass.
When designing a very large fusion, check its mass against the largest parent mass first; do not extrapolate beyond the parents without a flag.
When designing a very small fusion, check its mass against the smallest parent mass first; do not extrapolate below the parents without a flag.
When designing a fusion from a specimen measurement, label it as a specimen measurement, not a species range.
When designing a mythological fusion, list culture first, then components, then parts per component, in that order.
When designing a mythological fusion with a human part, flag it as mythology-only; human parts do not enter the species catalog.
When designing a shapeshifter, design both forms and the transition, not just the animal form.
When a design fails a hard rule, record the failure mode, the rule and the mitigation, and do not mark the design PASS.
When a design uses a blank trait, record the trait as unknown in the design, not as the most convenient value.
When a design is revised, keep the previous version's rule checks in the test log; do not overwrite history.
When designing a fusion with a stated brain_mass, keep it in grams and do not use it as a proxy for intelligence without a source.
When designing a fusion with a stated specimen mass, record the specimen's sex and sample size where the source gives them.
When designing a fusion that combines two parents from different classes (e.g. mammal x bird), flag it as a cross-class design, not a same-class fusion.
When designing a cross-class fusion, check body_plan, covering and movement separately; a shared diet does not make the plans compatible.
When designing a fusion with a marine parent, check salinity, depth and temperature, not just the word 'marine'.
When designing a fusion with a desert parent, check water, temperature and cover, not just the word 'desert'.
When designing a fusion with a nocturnal parent, check light, temperature and prey activity, not just the word 'nocturnal'.
When designing a fusion with a migratory parent, check seasonal habitat, not just the breeding habitat.
When designing a fusion with a venomous parent, record venom as a separate trait with its own donor; venom is not transferred by body plan alone.
When designing a fusion with a horned parent, record horn type (horn, antler, tusk) separately; they are different structures.
When fusing a serpentine parent with a quadruped parent, choose one body plan as primary and record the other as a trait note; do not record both as the body plan.
When fusing a multi-legged parent, state whether all legs are retained or a subset is used; a fusion with an unstated leg count is incomplete.
When fusing a shelled parent, state shell coverage by region; a shell that covers only the back is not a whole-body shell.
When fusing a winged parent, state wing span class (small, medium, large) from the parent's size class, not from a different bird.
When using a specimen mass in a fusion, copy its sex, sample size and reference into the fusion notes; a bare specimen mass is not a species mass.
When comparing a fusion's mass to a parent's, compare ranges to ranges and averages to averages; do not compare a range endpoint to an average as if they were the same kind of value.
When a parent's length is given only as a maximum, treat the fusion's length as unknown for that parent, not as the maximum.
When copying a real hybrid's fertility into a fusion, copy the sex-specific fertility if the source gives it; a single 'fertile' label hides male/female differences.
When a hybrid parent is itself a hybrid, draw the pedigree two generations deep in the design notes; a flat parent list hides the second generation.
When a hybrid shows heterosis, record the heterosis claim separately from mass; do not bake a larger mass into the fusion's mass interval silently.
When a fusion's parent glides, record glide as a movement token distinct from fly; powered flight and glide have different energy and control requirements.
When a fusion's parent burrows, record burrow as a movement token distinct from walk; burrowing requires a substrate note.
When parents differ in active_time, record the fusion's active_time as the overlap, or as a design choice with a note explaining the shift.
When a fusion uses a tundra|marine parent, record sea-ice dependence separately from cold tolerance; they are different constraints.
When a fusion uses a freshwater|marine parent, record life-stage habitat separately from adult habitat if the parent is anadromous.
When a fusion uses a broad-range parent, record the subset of habitats the fusion actually uses; do not copy the parent's full range.
When a fusion uses a carnivore|piscivore parent, record fish inclusion explicitly; do not assume all carnivores eat fish.
When a fusion uses an AnimalTraits metabolic value, record its specimen provenance; a watt value without sex, sample size and reference is not usable.
When a fusion uses an insectivore parent, record prey size class; small insects and large crustaceans are not interchangeable prey.
When a fusion uses a nine-component mythological creature, list all nine components' parts; a partial list is an incomplete design.
When a fusion uses a shapeshifting creature, design both forms and the shifting condition; a single form is not a shapeshifter design.
When a fusion uses a deity-creature, record deity status in the design notes; deity creatures are not ordinary animal composites.

definitions.about: Definitions of every field and value in 'animals'. Lists use '|' and mean the animal has all listed values. Activity terms are standard biology terms; 'unrecorded', 'radial' and 'bell' are project terms.

fields.animal_id: Unique snake_case key used to join every section.
fields.class / order / family: Taxonomic ranks from GBIF. Reptiles and ray-finned fish use the traditional classes Reptilia and Actinopterygii (see blank_notes on those rows).
fields.gbif_key: GBIF species key; taxonomy_url points to its API record.
fields.body_plan: Overall body layout. Values: quadruped (four walking legs), biped (two walking legs), winged (wings are the main limbs), finned (fins are the main limbs), multi_legged (six or more legs or arms), serpentine (long body, no limbs), radial (body arranged around a central axis with no front or back, as in jellyfish).
fields.primary_locomotor_part: Body part mainly used to move: four legs, two legs, multiple legs, wings, fins, flippers, bell (jellyfish swim by pulsing the bell-shaped body).
fields.covering: Outer body surface: fur, feathers, scales, skin (bare skin), exoskeleton (hard outer skeleton, as in insects and spiders), shell.
fields.movement: Ways the animal moves: walk, run, swim, fly, climb, burrow (digs through ground), glide (unpowered flight).
fields.active_time: When in the 24-hour day the animal is usually awake and active. See active_time_values.
fields.habitat: Places it lives: grassland, forest, mountain, tundra, wetland, freshwater, marine (sea), desert.
fields.climate: Climate zones it lives in: temperate, tropical, polar, arid.
fields.diet: Main food: carnivore (meat), herbivore (plants), omnivore (both), insectivore (insects), piscivore (fish).
fields.metabolic_rate_w: Basal or resting metabolic rate in watts.
fields.body_mass_kg: Adult body mass in kg. A range stays a range; midpoints are never computed.
fields.body_length_m: Adult body length in m. Same range rule as mass.
fields.blank_notes: Why a value is blank or unrecorded, and any project decisions on the row.
fields.source_url: Page the trait values came from.

active_time_values.diurnal: Active mainly during daylight, rests at night.
active_time_values.nocturnal: Active mainly at night, rests during the day.
active_time_values.crepuscular: Active mainly at dawn and dusk (twilight).
active_time_values.unrecorded: No source used here gave an activity period. Not a claim about the animal: it may be any pattern. Under rule R-A4-P04 it adds nothing to a fusion and never blocks one. Replace it with a sourced value when one is found.

definitions.active_time_combinations: A list such as 'diurnal|nocturnal' means the animal is recorded as active in each listed period. 'unrecorded' is always used alone.
